newsitem.title: UK: BAT seen lower as pressure on tobacco deal mounts.
newsitem.headline: BAT seen lower as pressure on tobacco deal mounts.

text.p: Shares in B.A.T. Industries Plc were expected to open lower on Thursday following news that the U.S. tobacco settlement was under pressure as public health groups rejected key parts of the deal.
By 0720 GMT, B.A.T. were indicated eight pence lower at 545p.

Comments from B.A.T. chief executive Martin Broughton, who said the settlement would not achieve drastic cuts in teenage smoking, could also damage the chances that the deal gets approval, the Financial Times newspaper said.
Broughton's comments could have reinforced the view of anti-smoking groups that the deal would benefit tobacco firms more than society, the newspaper said.
"It was clear that the pact would be challenged. So the uncertainty will prevail for the time until the whole thing is done", one analyst said.
Apart from the criticism of health groups, the Supreme Court's rejection of anasbestos litigation settlement could have repercussions for the tobacco deal.
The asbestos case had reinforced the view that the tobacco pact should be resolved through Congress and needed a nationwide claims processing system, legal experts said.
Analysts said that the asbestos case would only indirectly apply to B.A.T. but it had to be seen in a broader context.
"There will be a difficult and tortuous way to go to settle the accord", an analyst said.
Tobacco shares would remain depressed for a further six months but the upside for B.A.T. was enormous, the analyst said.
"B.A.T. will go north of seven pounds once the deal is sealed", he said.
